= GitHub Actions

This file describes how the workflows in `.github/workflows/` behave today.

Claude mention:: A maintainer's comment, review, or issue body that asks Claude to run.
Claude issue PR:: A pull request Claude opened for an issue, on a `claude-issue-<number>-...` branch.
Renovate PR:: A pull request that Renovate opened for one dependency.
Release issue:: An issue titled `Release @perfective/build vX.Y.Z`.
Publish PR:: The pull request from `publish-vX.Y.Z` that `publish-pr.yaml` opens for a release issue.

Every job runs on `ubuntu-latest`.
Jobs that install dependencies use Node `26.x`, except `ci.yaml`.
Jobs that run Claude read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and commit through the GitHub API.

== ci.yaml (Continuous Integration)

`ci.yaml` builds the package on every pull request, on a push to `main`, or on a push to a `vX.Y.x` branch.
The job runs once for Node versions `22.x`, `24.x`, and `26.x`.

== dependency-review.yaml (Dependency Review)

`dependency-review.yaml` runs a review by Claude when Renovate opens, reopens, and updates a Renovate PR;
or when the `claude-review` label is added to the PR.
Claude follows the `update-dependency` skill and may push one signed follow-up commit.
When the job succeeds, it triggers `codex-review.yaml`.

== claude.yaml (Claude)

`claude.yaml` runs on a Claude mention, or when a maintainer adds the `claude` label to an issue.
It skips release issues and Publish PRs, which `publish-pr.yaml` handles.
For an issue, Claude opens a Claude issue PR.
Ask for follow-ups on the Claude issue PR, where Claude continues on the same branch.
A run on the issue checks out `main` and cannot commit.
This workflow and `codex-review.yaml` share the concurrency group `claude-<number>`,
so only one of them pushes at a time.
`<number>` is the issue number for a Claude issue PR, and the pull request number otherwise.

== codex-review.yaml (Codex Review)

`codex-review.yaml` runs when Codex posts or edits its summary on a Renovate PR or a Claude issue PR,
and after `dependency-review.yaml` succeeds.
Each Codex review of a new commit is one round.
Claude fixes the open findings in rounds 1 and 2.
In round 3, the workflow only reports them.
When a review fails, or the workflow cannot read the summary, it comments and adds `help wanted`.

== codex-watchdog.yaml (Codex Review Watchdog)

`codex-watchdog.yaml` runs every hour, and a maintainer can run it by hand.
It checks open Renovate PRs and Claude issue PRs.
When the latest commit is at least two hours old and has no Codex review,
it comments and adds `help wanted`, once per commit.

== publish-pr.yaml (Publish PR)

`publish-pr.yaml` runs when a maintainer adds the `claude` label to an open release issue,
or writes a Claude mention on the Publish PR.
The job stops when the version's tag already exists, or when the Publish PR for that version is already merged.
If `publish-vX.Y.Z` already exists, Claude continues on it.
Claude commits one change titled `Publish vX.Y.Z`.
That commit may change only `package.json` (the version), `package-lock.json`, `CHANGELOG.adoc`,
`README.adoc`, `README.md`, and `ROADMAP.adoc`.
This workflow does not create the tag, and it does not publish to npm.

== publish.yaml (Publish)

`publish.yaml` publishes a new version of the package when a tag matching `v*` is pushed.
The tag must be annotated, GitHub must verify its signature, and the commit must be on `main` or on `vX.Y.x`.
`package.json` must carry that version, and `CHANGELOG.adoc` must contain a section for it.
The job runs `lint:build` and `dist`, then publishes `./dist` with provenance.
It signs in to npm with GitHub's OIDC token.
The npm dist-tag is one of the following:

* `next`, for a prerelease `vX.Y.Z-<id>`, on any branch
* `latest`, for any other release on `main`
* `backport-X.Y`, for any other release on `vX.Y.x`

This workflow does not create a GitHub Release; the maintainer creates it by hand.
Do not rename this file: npm trusted publishing is bound to the name `publish.yaml`.

== renovate.json

`renovate.json` makes Renovate open one pull request per dependency, with no automerge.
`rangeStrategy` is `bump`, so the version pin in `package.json` moves together with the lockfile.
A major update, a peer dependency update, and a TypeScript update receive the `help wanted` label.
The label `renovate-regenerate` tells Renovate to recreate the branch.
